Done. The kernel in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p48/round0/output_model_new.py) passes all 5 correctness trials and runs at 1.9ms vs 1.86ms for the reference PyTorch `torch.mean`.

The approach: a 2D grid where each thread handles one output element independently. Grid is `(batch_size, ceil(dim2 / 256), 1)` with 256 threads per block. Each thread loops over the full reduction dimension (4096 elements), accumulating bf16 values into an fp32 accumulator, then divides and stores back as bf16. No shared memory or warp synchronization needed, which kept the kernel simple and avoided the earlier OOM issues with 524K-block grids and complex shuffle reductions.
